- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.17) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially in early horizon.
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.28) or volatile, model often underestimates or overshoots after sharp moves; cap upward spikes and adjust downward if sentiment turns negative.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3-5 days), leading to overshoots in 30d forecast; apply smoothing or lagged decay to recent highs.
- When sentiment is flat (0.00) or near-zero, model often fails to capture mean reversion; add slight downward bias to mid-to-late horizon if no strong sentiment signal.
- If 30d forecast is >10% above true outcome and sentiment is neutral or positive, reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period to avoid overconfidence bias.
- If true outcome shows strong downward trend after a spike, model often fails to recognize it; apply “sentiment decay” rule: if sentiment drops below 0.05, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
